answer: Require each agent to earn a nontransferable reputation through repeated, independently audited work before it can claim rewards or influence allocations. Auditors sample tasks, compare outputs, and slash the bond of agents caught coordinating or fabricating results; newcomers gain weight only gradually. A sybil can still create many identities, but each must pay its own bond and accumulate a separate track record, making attacks costly in capital, time, and detectable failed work. A meadow of cheap accounts cannot instantly sway a mesa’s decisions or forge trust.
